title: Quota decomposition & journey mapping — per-key / per-route analytics
content:
Purpose: Capture a pragmatic set of UX sketches and backlog tasks that break down quota concepts into user-facing slices. Goal is to design an interface where engineers can: view how a quota is consumed across keys and routes, understand which traffic patterns are causing throttles, and take action (adjust quota, create exception, route fallback).

Context and motivation:
- Customers keep asking for per-key cost/usage transparency but also want to see what portion of a quota is used by specific routes (chat, embeddings, rerank). The current console surfaces global quotas and a per-key list; that isn't actionable when an app has many routes or multiplexed use.
- We want a single-page exploration that helps an engineer answer: "Is my token quota being eaten by a single noisy route?", "Did a rollout spike cause throttles for many keys?", "Which keys are near burst caps vs sustained quotas?"

High-level concept ("decomposition view"):
- Left pane: Key selector + quick summary cards. Selecting a key shows: total quota (daily/monthly), dollars remaining estimate, throttle count, 95th latency, top 5 routes by token consumption. Cards are tappable to flip to quick actions (increase quota, create temporary exception, open support case).
- Main canvas: Stacked timeline (heatmap) showing token consumption per-route over the selected period (default: 7d). Each layer is a route. Hover shows route name, tokens, requests, median latency. Top of timeline includes an overlay of "throttle events" as red ticks.
- Right pane: Breakdown + suggested remediations. Shows percent of quota consumed by route, percent of throttles attributable to route, and a small sparklines list for each route. Suggest remediation (auto-suggested) e.g., "Increase daily quota by 20% for route /api/v1/generate", "Enable burst allowance for key X between 08:00–10:00 PST". Suggestions are generated by heuristics (look for repeat patterns across 3+ days where route uses >40% of quota).

Wireframe details (interactions to prototype):
1) Key selector: typeahead with metadata chips (status: active/disabled, billing tier, owner email). Ability to multi-select keys for comparison (diff mode).
2) Timeline controls: timeframe quick picks (1h, 24h, 7d, 30d), aggregation granularity (1m/5m/1h). Toggle to view tokens vs requests vs cost.
3) Route drill-in: clicking a route removes other layers and expands a per-route panel with sample logs (anonymized), sample prompts (truncated), and example failure traces (rate-limited response). Button to open a support-prescribed Runbook (linked).
4) Throttle causality overlay: small checkbox to enable causality markers that attempt to correlate infra events (capacity loss, model fallback) with throttle spikes. Pulls from SRE incident log (linked).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Show per-key token/time series and stacked per-route decomposition for 7d (1h granularity).
- Heatmap shows throttle events as visible markers; clicking a marker filters the timeline to +/- 30m and shows top offending route(s).
- Right-pane suggestions surface at least 2 actionable options with links to the create-quota API and to open a support ticket.
- Multi-select keys for side-by-side comparison (at least 2 keys).
- No PII shown in sample prompts; logs are anonymized.

Backlog grooming (epic -> stories, rough estimates):
EPIC: quota-decomposition-explore (JIRA-RT-789)
- Story 1 (3): backend API: aggregated per-route token metrics (time series) + throttle event markers. (RT-790)
- Story 2 (5): UI: stacked timeline component with hover/tooltip. (RT-791)
- Story 3 (5): key selector and multi-select diff mode. (RT-792)
- Story 4 (3): right-pane suggestion engine (heuristics only) + UI list. (RT-793)
- Story 5 (2): route drill-in panel + sample anonymized logs. (RT-794)
- Story 6 (2): plumbing for incident correlation overlay (reads SRE event stream). (RT-795)
- Spike (1): data volume / perf test for 30d stacked render; verify smart downsampling. (RT-796)
Total: 21 points (sprint friendly: split across 2 sprints).

Design trade-offs & open questions:
- Downsampling vs fidelity: rendering many routes across long windows is heavy. MVP will cap routes to top 10 by volume with an option to "show more". Edge case: a set of many small routes add up to a large percent; we should surface "other routes" band.
- Cost vs data retention: 30d full-fidelity could be expensive. Suggest storing 1h rollups after 7d. Need analytics input (Product Ops).
- Suggestions accuracy and safety: heuristic-based suggestions are easy to ship, but we must avoid auto-increasing quotas without explicit user action. Suggested action must require confirm and show cost delta estimate.
- Role controls: Only billing owners or admins can change quota. Design must show disabled controls + guided path to request change.

Small UI copy samples (for prototyping):
- Decomposition header: "How this key is using your quota"
- Suggestion card: "Increase daily quota for /api/v1/generate — estimated +$12/day"
- Throttle marker tooltip: "Throttle spike — 245 requests rate-limited at 2026-02-18T09:12Z"

Prototype tasks (UX):
- Low-fi wireframe screens: key list, stacked timeline, suggestion drawer, route drill (2 screens each). Owner: Sofia. Due: 2025-11-15.
- Clickable prototype (Figma): add interactions for hover, multi-select, and suggestion flow. Owner: Jordan. Due: 2025-11-22.
- Usability test plan: recruit 5 platform engineers (internal) to run 20-minute tasks. Scripts to include: identify throttle cause, propose action, compare 2 keys. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2025-11-29.

Metrics to evaluate success:
- Time-to-resolution: median time engineers take to identify throttle cause drops by 40% in internal tests.
- Adoption: percentage of keys with at least one decomposition view opened within 14 days after release (target 20%).
- Suggestion conversion: percent of UI suggestions that lead to user action (target 15% within 30 days).

Open follow-ups (post-MVP):
- Auto-generated guardrails: recommend automated rate-limit exceptions for scheduled jobs (cron) with a safety window.
- Integration with Optimize: provide quantization/batch recommendations tied to route patterns.
- Export: CSV/Notebook export of per-route breakdown for offline analysis.

Unresolved decisions to bring to PM sync:
- SLA for rollouts: should non-admins be able to request temporary quota increases that auto-approve for <1h?
- Cost estimation model: how to include downstream costs (dedicated infra) in suggestion math.

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus review on the core exploration flow: key selection -> timeline -> route drill -> suggestion.
- Look out for edge cases where route names are dynamic (UUIDs); we need normalization rules.
- Please annotate where integrations with SRE/usage-cost APIs are missing.

Attachments / mock screenshots referenced: none yet — low-fi accepted.

Last quick wins to consider before first demo:
- Add a "Top offending routes" mini-card on the key list screen (fast to add, high signal).
- Show a cost delta tooltip when hovering over suggestion cards.
- Add query param support so engineering flows can deep-link into a specific key + time window.

End of document.
